correctness.rationale: Exact expectation decomposition (1), bias identity (2), and RR finite-population formula (3) were rederived with all indices and quantifiers. The full sample-mask quadratic form decomposes into trivial and block-contrast representations, its top eigenvalue is the 2x2 formula, and Sylvester criterion plus a convex quadratic polynomial proves the strict partial-prefix bound. Exact permutation enumerations and rational principal-minor checks passed 8260 tests from the supplied CHECK.py; finite checks are supplementary.

originality.rationale: Best-knowledge originality: the arXiv:2604.00260v1 full-text propositions treat whole blocks as sampling units and the usual RR finite-population lemma. Whole-cluster design effects are known and not claimed new. The assessed mathematical extension is the complete sharp per-individual-prefix eigenvalue law with order bias, equality and strict partial-block gap. Full relevant primary sections were inspected; remaining older partially filled cluster theory is a real bibliographic risk.
residual_risks: An earlier survey-sampling text may give the same sharp partially completed cluster design-effect spectrum under equivalent terminology; some relevant classical texts were not inspected in full.

value.rationale: Complete natural classification of every gradient-prefix sampling budget in fixed-order block shuffling: exact sharp variance inflation, a nontrivial incomplete-block spectral profile and bias, strictness versus whole-block endpoints, and the exact between/within-block comparison criterion. The construction responds to a current numerical-optimization design question while carefully excluding classical whole-block identities and any unproved convergence/runtime implications.
